reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and holiday adjustment helpers, but duplicates the skip-versus-move policy instead of sharing it across consumers.

duplication.why: Holiday matching is centralized, but daily occurrence handling is duplicated between getNextDate and getAdjustedOccurrence, and budget adjustment remains repeated.

placement.why: The handler belongs in the schedules server module, but its occurrence-adjustment policy belongs alongside the shared scheduling logic.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate policy changes across shared scheduling, server adjustment, and budget orchestration, while the new handler also leaves config untyped despite RecurConfig existing.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts: getAdjustedOccurrence independently implements the occurrence policy also implemented by shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: getAdjustedOccurrence expresses the same daily skip/non-daily move decision as getNextDate through early returns rather than filtering and conditional adjustment.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter; getNextDate gains daily filtering and non-daily adjustment conditions; getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange use a separate server-local policy implementation.
